title: SIP — Systematic Investment Plan, explained simply
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: A SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) lets you invest a fixed amount in a mutual fund every month, like a recurring deposit but for market-linked funds. You can start with as little as ₹100 to ₹500 a month in many funds. Because you buy every month, you get more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high — this is called rupee-cost averaging, and it removes the stress of timing the market. SIPs work best over 5 years or more, because equity funds can fall sharply in the short term. Returns are not guaranteed and can be negative. You can pause or stop a SIP at any time; there is no penalty from the SIP itself, though some funds charge an exit load if you redeem early.
summary_hinglish: SIP matlab har mahine ek fixed amount mutual fund mein invest karna, ₹100-500 se bhi shuru ho sakta hai. Market upar-neeche hota rehta hai to average cost balance ho jaata hai. Kam se kam 5 saal ke liye socho, aur returns guaranteed nahi hote.
summary_hi: SIP यानी हर महीने एक तय रकम म्यूचुअल फंड में निवेश करना, ₹100-500 से भी शुरू हो सकता है। इससे बाज़ार के उतार-चढ़ाव में औसत लागत संतुलित रहती है। कम से कम 5 साल के लिए सोचें; रिटर्न की गारंटी नहीं होती।
